whyCorrect: Split the fraction: \(\frac{2a+b}{b}=\frac{2a}{b}+\frac{b}{b}=2\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)+1\). Substituting \(\frac{a}{b}=\frac{5}{3}\) gives \(\frac{10}{3}+1=\frac{13}{3}\). You can check with a = 5 and b = 3: \(\frac{10+3}{3}=\frac{13}{3}\).

whyWrong.A: \(\frac{8}{3}\) is \(\frac{a+b}{b}\), which leaves out the doubling of a.
whyWrong.B: \(\frac{10}{3}\) is \(\frac{2a}{b}\) with the \(\frac{b}{b}=1\) never added.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{13}{5}\) divides by a instead of b, turning the ratio upside down.

commonMistakes: Trying to solve for a and b separately; only their ratio is fixed, and only the ratio is needed.
tips: Pick convenient values matching the ratio, such as a = 5 and b = 3, and evaluate directly as a check.

whyCorrect: A parabola takes each value twice, once on each side of its axis of symmetry, and the axis here is \(x=-\frac{-8}{2}=4\). The input 2 sits 2 units left of the axis, so its partner sits 2 units right, at x = 6. Check: f(2) = 4 - 16 + 21 = 9 and f(6) = 36 - 48 + 21 = 9.

whyWrong.B: 5 gives f(5) = 25 - 40 + 21 = 6; it is the partner of 3, not of 2.
whyWrong.D: 10 comes from using -b = 8 as the axis instead of \(-\frac{b}{2a}=4\), and f(10) = 41.

commonMistakes: Solving the full quadratic \(x^{2}-8x+21=9\) is fine but slower; the symmetry gives the partner directly.
tips: The two inputs sharing an output are always equidistant from the axis, so their average is the axis.

whyCorrect: Convert both means into totals. The original 8 times total 8(34) = 272 seconds, and the 10 times total 10(39.2) = 392. So the two added times come to 392 - 272 = 120 seconds, and the other one is 120 - 58 = 62.

whyWrong.A: 58 would make the two added times total 116, giving a mean of 38.8 rather than 39.2.
whyWrong.B: 60 would total 118 and give a mean of 39.0.
whyWrong.D: 66 would total 124 and give a mean of 39.6.

commonMistakes: Halving the 120 to 60 as if both added times were equal.
tips: Any "mean changed by adding values" question becomes arithmetic once every mean is turned into a sum.

whyCorrect: The plate is chosen from the usable ones, so the denominator is the usable total: 84 + 96 + 60 = 240. Of those, 84 came from the astrograph, so the probability is \(\frac{84}{240}=\frac{7}{20}\).

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{6}{25}\) is \(\frac{84}{350}\), the chance that a plate drawn from all 350 plates is both usable and from the astrograph.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{21}{50}\) is 0.42, which would need a denominator of 200 — no group in the table has that size.
whyWrong.D: \(\frac{42}{125}\) is 0.336, corresponding to 84 out of 250, again a total that appears nowhere in the table.

commonMistakes: Using the grand total when the question has already restricted the pool to one row or column.
tips: "One of the usable plates is selected" fixes the denominator before you read any other number.

whyCorrect: Apply the changes in order to the running total, not to the original. The second year is 5,000(1.06) = 5,300, and the third is 5,300(0.94) = 4,982 kilograms. The 6% fall is taken from the larger amount, so it removes more than the rise added.

whyWrong.A: 4,964 removes about twice the actual net loss; the combined factor is 1.06(0.94) = 0.9964, not 0.9928.
whyWrong.C: 5,000 assumes a rise and a fall of the same percentage cancel, which they do not because the bases differ.
whyWrong.D: 5,018 has the net change in the wrong direction — a rise then an equal-percentage fall always ends below the start.

commonMistakes: Adding and subtracting 6% of 5,000, which treats the second year's base as unchanged.
tips: Multiply the factors together first: 1.06(0.94) = 0.9964, a net fall of 0.36%.

whyCorrect: Work in minutes. 3 hours 20 minutes is 200 minutes, and 200 prints in 200 minutes is exactly 1 print a minute. 5 hours 15 minutes is 315 minutes, so the printer turns out 315 prints.

whyWrong.A: 252 is what 4 hours 12 minutes would produce.
whyWrong.B: 280 corresponds to 4 hours 40 minutes.
whyWrong.C: 300 drops the extra 15 minutes and counts only the 5 whole hours.

commonMistakes: Reading "3 hours 20 minutes" as 3.2 hours; 20 minutes is a third of an hour, not two tenths.
tips: Convert every mixed time to a single unit before setting up the proportion.

whyCorrect: Removing three unexposed plates changes both counts. The unexposed left are 15 - 3 = 12, and the plates left in the drawer are 40 - 3 = 37. So the probability is \(\frac{12}{37}\), which does not reduce.
commonMistakes: Changing the numerator to 12 but leaving the denominator at 40, which forgets that the drawer itself is now smaller.
tips: When items are removed, update the total as well as the favourable count.

whyCorrect: The legs are AB, which runs from x = -3 to x = 5 for a length of 8, and BC, which runs from y = 2 to y = 8 for a length of 6. So the hypotenuse AC is \(\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}=10\). The midpoint of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is equidistant from all three vertices, so BM is half of AC, which is 5. Directly: M is (1, 5), and \(BM=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5\).

whyWrong.A: 3 is half of the vertical leg BC, not half of the hypotenuse.
whyWrong.B: 4 is half of the horizontal leg AB.
whyWrong.D: 6 is the length of leg BC itself.

commonMistakes: Halving a leg instead of the hypotenuse, or computing the midpoint of the wrong side.
tips: In any right triangle, the distance from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse's midpoint is half the hypotenuse.

whyCorrect: The curved surface of a hemisphere is \(2\pi r^{2}\), so \(2\pi r^{2}=72\pi\) gives \(r^{2}=36\) and r = 6. The volume of a hemisphere is half a sphere's: \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}=\frac{2}{3}\pi(216)=144\pi\) cubic metres.

whyWrong.A: \(72\pi\) repeats the given surface area as if it were the volume.
whyWrong.B: \(108\pi\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi r^{3}\), halving \(\pi r^{3}\) instead of using \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}\).
whyWrong.D: \(288\pi\) is the volume of the whole sphere of radius 6, not the hemisphere.

commonMistakes: Using \(4\pi r^{2}\) for the curved surface, which is a full sphere and gives r = \(3\sqrt{2}\).
tips: Find r from the area first; every later formula is a substitution once you have it.

whyCorrect: With the right angle at B, angles A and C add to 90 degrees, so they are complementary. The side adjacent to A is AB, and that same side is opposite C, so \(\cos A\) and \(\sin C\) are the same ratio: both equal \(\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{7}{25}\).

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{7}{24}\) is \(\tan A\), the ratio of the two legs rather than a leg to the hypotenuse.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{24}{25}\) is \(\sin A\), which equals \(\cos C\) — the complementary pair the other way round.
whyWrong.D: \(\frac{25}{7}\) inverts the ratio, and a sine can never exceed 1.

commonMistakes: Assuming \(\sin C\) must be the "other" ratio, 24/25, because the letters differ.
tips: In a right triangle the sine of one acute angle always equals the cosine of the other.

whyCorrect: The volume is base area times height, so the base area is 12,000/30 = 400 square centimetres, making the square base 20 by 20. The felt covers the base, 400 square centimetres, plus four walls each 20 by 30, which is 4(600) = 2,400. Altogether that is 400 + 2,400 = 2,800 square centimetres.
commonMistakes: Adding a top as well, which the open tank does not have, or using 400 as the side length instead of the area.
tips: Take the square root of the base area to recover the side before computing any wall.
